message.reasoning_content:
Describe the kernel. Key risk spots: the packed-real-FFT reconstruction math, the Nyquist bin store, the twiddle table sign folding, bit-reversal, and the real-FFT identity check. Let me quickly reason.

Packed trick: treat x[2j]+i x[2j+1] as complex signal of length M=N/2, compute F[k] = A[k]. Then real FFT bins: X[k] = Re(A[k]+conj(A[-k])e^{-2πik/N})... Standard: X[k] = 0.5[(A[k]+conj(A[M-k])) - i e^{-2πi2k... }]. Not going to fully verify; record as risk.

Nyquist bin (k=M, N/2): stored as ar - ai at masked store where address from k==0 address = reverse(0)=0, partner = 0. So ar,ai are F[0] = sum x even... Actually Nyquist X[N/2] = sum_j (-1)^j x[j]. Kernel stores ar - ai where ar=Re F[0], ai=Im F[0]: F[0]=sum (x[2j]+i x[2j+1]) so Re=sum even, Im=sum odd; Re-Im = sum even - sum odd = sum (-1)^j x[j]. Correct.

Also check frequency k range 0..M-1 handled in loop; correct if reconstruction formula right. Note _twiddle: phase from 0..127; folded=min(phase,128-phase) — for phase up to 127 fine. twiddle returns cos, -sin (e^{-iθ})? cosθ - i sinθ? -sine where sine=cos(64-phase table)... table[p]=cos(2πp/256), abs(64-phase) index: cos(|64-phase|*2π/256)=cos(π/2 - 2πphase/256)=sin(2πphase/256). OK so returns (cos θ, -sin θ), i.e. e^{-iθ}. Standard FFT convention.
